quiz.q: According to the social constructivist perspective, why was the Cold War considered not inevitable?
options: It stemmed from mutual misperceptions, miscalculations, and missed diplomatic opportunities rather than structural necessity.
It was driven strictly by irreconcilable conflicts between the core national interests of both superpowers.
It was solely caused by Soviet ideological expansionism and aggressive military posturing in Eastern Europe.
It resulted entirely from American economic imperialism seeking to impose global capitalist hegemony after war.
quiz.why: Social constructivists argue that the Cold War was not structurally predetermined, but arose from mutual miscalculations and missed diplomatic opportunities.

quiz.q: According to Nina Tannenwald, why did the United States refrain from using nuclear weapons in Vietnam?
options: Strategic parity made conventional air tactics far more cost-effective against widespread dispersed guerrilla forces.
International arms control treaties legally prohibited superpowers from deploying nuclear weapons in regional conflicts.
A normative taboo and public pressure made the use of nuclear weapons politically unacceptable.
Soviet retaliatory capabilities in Southeast Asia created an immediate danger of mutual assured destruction.
quiz.why: Nina Tannenwald highlights that an evolving normative taboo and moral public pressure prevented leaders from deploying nuclear weapons.

quiz.q: How does the study of Cold War diplomacy characterize the period of 'Detente'?
options: A permanent ideological reconciliation that officially ended systemic competition between capitalism and communism.
A temporary relaxation of geopolitical tensions without any qualitative transformation in adversarial relations.
A comprehensive military alliance designed to jointly manage and de-escalate Third World conflicts.
A complete dismantling of global nuclear arsenals achieved through binding bilateral disarmament treaties.
quiz.why: Detente represented a temporary relaxation of diplomatic tensions and arms competition rather than a qualitative transformation in fundamental relations.

quiz.q: How does Alexis de Tocqueville's insight explain the disintegration of the Soviet Union under Gorbachev?
options: Authoritarian regimes collapse immediately when global commodity prices drop and economic growth stagnates.
External military encirclement inevitably forces closed socialist systems to disintegrate from economic exhaustion.
Popular mass rebellions only erupt when tyrannical governments reach their absolute peak of repression.
Totalitarian states face their greatest vulnerability when they attempt to reform their oppressive structures.
quiz.why: Tocqueville noted that the most perilous moment for an oppressive regime occurs when it begins to introduce liberalizing reforms.
